mainTopic: A woman's milk and טומאה; the איסור for a כהן to drink wine before the עבודה and for anyone to rule after drinking; and one act of eating that brings many korbanot.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about the fluids of a זב and זבה. Because a woman's milk only gives ordinary טומאת משקין with a רביעית, the גמרא concludes that milk does not come from a מעיין. It then explains that the משנה's phrase 'not wanted' means only that the baby gave no sign, since babies naturally want milk. Next, the גמרא explains the משנה about a כהן who ate or drank before entering the מקדש. A ברייתא gives three readings of 'יין ושכר אל תשת': the תנא קמא, רבי יהודה (who includes other intoxicants), and רבי אלעזר (only wine drunk the intoxicating way). The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר, and a story with רב אשי limits his leniency to a רביעית. Another ברייתא lists which kinds of teaching are forbidden after drinking wine, and רב rules like רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that only actual rulings are forbidden. Finally, a new משנה shows how one act of eating can bring four חטאות and one אשם, and רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue over adding carrying on שבת.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: milk versus saliva and discharge
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying a woman's milk gives ordinary liquid טומאה with a רביעית, while saliva, discharge and urine give severe טומאה in any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a woman's milk makes things impure with the impurity of liquids, if there is a quarter-לוג. His saliva, his discharge and his urine make things impure with severe impurity, in any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting on the previous page. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits the fluids into two groups. Milk is in the lighter group: it needs a רביעית and only gives טומאת משקין. Saliva, discharge and urine are in the severe group and are מטמא in any amount.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's milk
The ordinary impurity of a liquid
A quarter-log, a set measure of liquid
Severe impurity, like that of an אב הטומאה
In any amount at all, even a tiny bit

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think milk is pure here. It is still מטמא, just with the lighter liquid טומאה and only with a רביעית.

phrases.english: and the milk of a woman
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ברייתא from the previous page that lists the fluids of a זבה.

phrases.english: transmit impurity of liquids with a quarter-log.
His saliva, his discharge, and his urine
phrases.notes: "His" means a זב.

phrases.english: transmit severe impurity, in any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲלֵב אִשָּׁה מְטַמְּאִין טוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין בִּרְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted at the end of the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's milk gives טומאת משקין only with a רביעית. Saliva, discharge and urine give severe טומאה in any amount.

steps.title: If milk came from a spring, it should be severe
steps.stepSummary: If the place of milk were a מעיין, milk should be in the severe group, just like discharge and saliva.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the place of the milk is a spring, then milk too should make things impure with severe impurity in any amount, just like his discharge and his saliva!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to attack רבא's idea that the place of milk counts as a מעיין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the breast were a מעיין, milk would be a fluid coming straight from a source in the body, like discharge and saliva. Then it should share their severe טומאה. But the ברייתא puts milk in the lighter group.

keyTerms.meaning: The place the milk comes from
A spring, a natural source
And if you say (the start of a challenge)

phrases.english: And if you say the place of milk is a spring,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. This is רבא's view from the previous page.

phrases.english: then milk too should transmit severe impurity
in any amount, like his discharge and his saliva!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ מְקוֹם חָלָב מְעַיֵּין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from Step 1 to challenge רבא's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the place of a woman's milk is a מעיין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were a מעיין, milk would match discharge and saliva and be severe in any amount. The ברייתא says it is not.

steps.title: So the place of milk is not a spring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the place of a woman's milk is not a מעיין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the place of a woman's milk is not a spring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the challenge: milk does not come from a מעיין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא treats milk more lightly than discharge and saliva, its source cannot be a מעיין. Milk is treated like an ordinary liquid that needs הכשר, meaning it must be wanted, to count as a liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, we can conclude
Not

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion: מקום חלב אשה לאו מעיין הוא. A woman's milk does not come from a 'spring.'

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם חֲלֵב אִשָּׁה לָאו מַעְיָין הוּא.
phrases.english: the place of a woman's milk is not a spring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the challenge in Step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The place of a woman's milk is not considered a מעיין.

steps.title: Then what about the משנה רבא quoted?
steps.stepSummary: If milk is not from a מעיין, the משנה רבא cited is hard to explain, since it says milk is מטמא even when not wanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this משנה that רבא cited is difficult: 'It makes things impure whether wanted or not wanted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new conclusion with the משנה רבא had used as his support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A liquid normally only makes food ready for טומאה if it is wanted (לרצון). If milk is an ordinary liquid, it should need to be wanted. But the משנה says it works even 'not wanted,' which sounded like milk is special.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It is difficult
A משנה or ברייתא, here the משנה רבא cited
Wanted, to one's satisfaction

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not wanted' here does not yet mean 'unwanted.' The next step explains what it really means.

phrases.english: If so, this משנה is difficult,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מכשירין that רבא cited on the previous page.

phrases.english: which Rava cited:
"it renders impure whether wanted or not wanted"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the place of milk is not a מעיין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ordinary liquids must be wanted to make food ready for טומאה, yet the משנה says milk works even when not wanted.

steps.title: 'Not wanted' means no clear sign either way
steps.stepSummary: 'Not wanted' means the baby gave no sign. Since a baby naturally wants milk, that counts as wanted. If he clearly does not want it, the milk is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think 'not wanted' means he does not want it? No. 'Not wanted' means he gave no sign, because a baby's mind is drawn to milk. But if he shows he does not want it, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה's words 'not wanted' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not wanted' does not mean the baby rejected the milk. It means he gave no clear sign. A baby naturally likes milk, so we assume he wants it. If he clearly does not want it, the milk stays טהור, just like any ordinary liquid, so the conclusion of Step 3 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (introducing a wrong assumption)
He does not want it
His mind is drawn close to it
Pure

steps.whatToRemember: A woman's milk is an ordinary liquid that needs to be wanted. A baby is assumed to want milk unless he clearly shows he does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the משנה while keeping the conclusion that milk is not from a מעיין.

phrases.english: Do you think that "not wanted," which it says,
means he does not want it?
No. What does "not wanted," which it says, mean?
That a baby's mind is drawn to milk,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמַר לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ – טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: but if he shows he does not want it, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not wanted' means the baby rejected the milk, so milk would work even without being wanted.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not wanted' means no clear sign. A baby is assumed to want milk. If he clearly rejects it, the milk is טהור.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need him to 'remain'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about someone who ate impure food or drank wine and asks why the word 'ושהה' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He ate impure foods, etc.' Why do I need 'remaining', since the משנה says 'and he remained'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks why it needs the word 'ושהה', 'and he remained'. Once he entered the מקדש in that state, he should be חייב right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'ושהה' means he stayed inside the מקדש for some time, it seems like an extra condition that makes no sense. The very act of entering should be enough. So the גמרא is asking what this word really means.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asks why a word or detail is needed)
Remaining, spending time
And he remained (the word in the משנה being asked about)

phrases.english: He ate impure foods, etc.
Why do I need remaining,
that it teaches: 'and he remained'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It quotes a new line of the משנה about entering the מקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Entering the מקדש while impure or after drinking wine should make him חייב right away. Needing him to stay a while seems pointless.

steps.title: 'Remaining' means the time spent eating and drinking
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that 'ושהה' refers to how long he took to eat or drink: no more than כדי אכילת פרס. Then he entered the מקדש and is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה means. He ate impure foods, or drank impure liquids, or drank a רביעית of wine, and he took the time of eating a פרס to eat or drink them. Then he entered the מקדש, and he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that 'ושהה' does not mean staying in the מקדש. It means how long he took while eating or drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he ate or drank the full amount within כדי אכילת פרס, it all joins together as one act of eating or drinking. So the word 'ושהה' is not an extra condition for being inside the מקדש. It sets the time limit for the eating and drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to teach (a rereading of the משנה)
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf; the time limit for joining together
A quarter of a לוג, a set measure for liquids
Liable, deserving the punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'ושהה' as 'he stayed in the מקדש.' Here it means how long he took to eat or drink, before he entered.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it is teaching:
he ate impure foods,
or drank impure liquids,
or drank a quarter-log of wine,
and he spent, in eating them and drinking them,
the time of eating a half-loaf,
and then entered the Temple – he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה (הכי קתני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ושהה' means he stayed inside the מקדש for some time.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ושהה' means he finished eating or drinking within כדי אכילת פרס. Then entering the מקדש makes him חייב.

steps.title: Does the פסוק forbid even a tiny amount, or fresh wine?
steps.stepSummary: After quoting רבי אלעזר in the משנה, the גמרא brings a ברייתא on 'יין ושכר אל תשת'. It first raises the possibility that even any amount, or fresh unfermented wine, is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'רבי אלעזר says, etc.' The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: 'Do not drink wine or שכר.' You might think this means even any amount, and even wine straight from its press?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to רבי אלעזר's part of the משנה and brings a ברייתא about the פסוק. The ברייתא opens with a possible way to read the פסוק, which it will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא suggests reading the פסוק very broadly: any drop of wine, even new wine that has not fermented yet. This is a 'יכול', a first guess that the ברייתא sets up so it can limit it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think (a first guess that will be limited)
Any amount, even the smallest
From its press: fresh wine that has not fermented yet
An intoxicating drink

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה. There רבי אלעזר says that if he stopped in the middle of drinking, or mixed any water into the wine, he is פטור.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'Do not drink wine or intoxicating drink' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:9

phrases.english: you might think: even any amount,
even straight from its press?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ כֹּל שֶׁהוּא, אֲפִילּוּ מִגִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the part of the משנה with רבי אלעזר and the source in the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the פסוק forbid any amount of wine, even unfermented wine from the press?

steps.title: 'שכר' limits it to an amount that can make you drunk
steps.stepSummary: The word 'שכר' teaches that the איסור is only for an amount that can make you drunk: a רביעית of wine at least forty days old.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'ושכר'. That teaches it is forbidden only when there is enough to make a person drunk. How much is enough to make a person drunk? A רביעית of wine that is forty days old.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own guess. The word 'שכר', meaning intoxicating, shows the איסור is about wine that can make you drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two limits come from this word. The amount must be at least a רביעית. The wine must be at least forty days old, after it has fermented. So a small amount or new wine is not included in this main איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
Enough to make someone drunk
Forty days old: wine that has fermented

phrases.english: The verse states: 'or intoxicating drink' –
it is forbidden only when it is enough to make drunk,
and how much is enough to make drunk?
A quarter-log of wine that is forty days old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the guess of step 8 by limiting the איסור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only an amount that can make you drunk is forbidden: a רביעית of wine at least forty days old.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say 'wine'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'שכר' already teaches the rule, the word 'יין' seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'wine'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק needs the word 'יין', since 'שכר' already covered everything. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'שכר' gave us the amount and the age of the wine, the word 'יין' looks extra. An extra word in a פסוק must be there to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what we just said is true)
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Wine: the word that seems extra

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say 'wine'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of step 9: if 'שכר' teaches everything, 'יין' is extra.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'שכר' already gave the full rule, so 'יין' seems to add nothing.

steps.title: 'Wine' teaches that even a little, or fresh wine, is still forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יין' teaches that a person is warned against even any amount of wine, and even wine straight from the press.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is there to tell you that people are warned about it even in any amount, and they are warned about it even straight from the press.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'יין' adds a wider איסור. Small amounts and new wine are forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there are two levels. The full איסור of 'שכר' needs a רביעית of wine at least forty days old. The word 'יין' adds a warning (מוזהרין) against any amount and against fresh wine as well. Both limits from step 9 are now covered by a lower-level איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: To tell you (introduces what the extra word teaches)
They are warned: there is an איסור
About it (about the wine)

steps.whatToRemember: 'שכר' sets the full איסור: a רביעית of wine forty days old. 'יין' adds that even any amount, or fresh wine from the press, is still forbidden before entering the מקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the משנה can make the main liability depend on a full רביעית, while smaller amounts are still not allowed.

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לְךָ שֶׁמּוּזְהָרִין עָלָיו כֹּל שֶׁהוּא,
phrases.english: to tell you that they are warned about it even in any amount,
phrases.notes: 'Warned' means it is still forbidden, even though it is not the full level of איסור that 'שכר' teaches.

phrases.english: and they are warned about it even straight from its press.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לְךָ שֶׁמּוּזְהָרִין עָלָיו כֹּל שֶׁהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by giving the extra word 'יין' its own teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word its own teaching
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יין' teaches a warning against any amount and against fresh wine, beyond the main רביעית rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There are two levels: the full איסור needs a רביעית of wine forty days old, and there is still an איסור on any amount and on fresh wine.

steps.title: רבי יהודה asks where other intoxicating drinks are included
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the word 'יין' alone would teach only about wine, and asks what source includes other intoxicating drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: From 'wine' I would only know about wine. Where do we learn that other intoxicating drinks are included?
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא, רבי יהודה, gives his own reading of the פסוק. He opens by asking how we know that drinks other than wine are forbidden, which sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treated both words as being about wine. רבי יהודה starts from a different place: 'יין' covers wine only. So he needs another word in the פסוק to cover all other intoxicating drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (this case, and nothing more)
intoxicating drinks
from where do we learn it?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"Wine": I have only wine,
from where do we know other intoxicating drinks?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא יַיִן, שְׁאָר מְשַׁכְּרִין מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second opinion in the same ברייתא, different from the תנא קמא in steps 8-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that includes intoxicating drinks other than wine.

steps.title: The word 'ושכר' includes other intoxicating drinks
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ושכר' teaches that other intoxicating drinks are also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'and intoxicating drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers his own question: the word 'ושכר' is the source for all other intoxicating drinks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, 'שכר' means a different drink from wine. This is different from the תנא קמא, who used 'שכר' to define how much wine and how old it must be.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק teaches (by saying)
intoxicating drink

steps.confusionAlert: The same word 'שכר' was used in step 9 to define a measure of wine. Here רבי יהודה uses it for a completely different job: adding new kinds of drinks.

phrases.english: The verse states: "and intoxicating drink."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק still need the word 'wine'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'שכר' covers all intoxicating drinks, wine is already included, so the word 'יין' looks extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק need to say 'wine'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges רבי יהודה's reading. If 'שכר' already includes every intoxicating drink, wine should be covered too, so why mention it separately?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. Once 'שכר' is read broadly, 'יין' seems to add nothing, so it must be teaching something special about wine.

keyTerms.meaning: if so

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse state "wine"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad reading of 'שכר' from step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'שכר' covers all intoxicants, then wine is already included and 'יין' is extra.

steps.title: Wine brings death; other drinks are only a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: 'יין' is mentioned to teach that only wine carries the punishment of מיתה. Other drinks carry only an אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For wine, the punishment is death. For other drinks, there is only a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'יין' is needed to set wine apart: a כהן who enters after drinking wine is חייב מיתה, but after other drinks he only breaks a prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of drinks are forbidden. But the death punishment in the end of the פסוק ('ולא תמתו') is limited to wine, which the פסוק names on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: death (here, at the hands of Heaven)
a prohibition (a warning), without the death punishment

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a two-level system: wine is more severe than other intoxicants, though both are forbidden.

phrases.english: For wine, the punishment is death,
and for other drinks, only a prohibition.
phrases.notes: He means other intoxicating drinks. They are still forbidden, just without the death punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל הַיַּיִן – בְּמִיתָה, וְעַל שְׁאָר מַשְׁקִין – בְּאַזְהָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a new teaching (a difference in punishment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יין' seems extra, since 'שכר' already covers wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יין' limits the death punishment to wine; other intoxicants are only an אזהרה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: forbidden only when drunk in the intoxicating way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads the פסוק as 'do not drink wine in the way that intoxicates.' If one paused while drinking or added any water, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: 'Do not drink wine and intoxicating drink' means do not drink it the way it makes you drunk. But if he stopped in the middle, or put even a little water into it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא gives his reading. For רבי אלעזר, 'שכר' is not a separate drink. It describes how the wine is drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only wine drunk in one go and undiluted is forbidden. Drinking with a pause, or mixing in any water at all, removes the חיוב.

keyTerms.meaning: in the way it makes one drunk
he paused (stopped in the middle of drinking)
any amount at all
exempt

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying diluted wine is allowed in general. He is only saying a כהן is not חייב for it under this פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
"Wine you shall not drink, and intoxicating drink":
phrases.notes: He reads the פסוק as one idea: wine, drunk in a way that intoxicates.

phrases.english: do not drink it in the manner that it intoxicates,
but if he paused in drinking it,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ נָתַן לְתוֹכוֹ מַיִם כֹּל שֶׁהוּא –
phrases.english: or put any amount of water into it,
he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: ״יַיִן אַל תֵּשְׁתְּ וְשֵׁכָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third reading of the same פסוק within the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One is חייב only for drinking wine in its intoxicating manner. If he paused, or added any water, he is פטור.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying point the three תנאים disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא itself speaks, not the ברייתא. It asks what causes the three opinions to read the פסוק so differently, which sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is to find the one key idea behind each view, so the opinions are not just three random readings.

keyTerms.meaning: about what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back to analyze all the views in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for the מחלוקת among the תנא קמא, רבי יהודה, and רבי אלעזר.

steps.title: The תנא קמא learns 'שכר' from נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'שכר' in the parsha of נזיר, where it refers to wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds: we learn the word 'שכר' here from the word 'שכר' said about a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the תנא קמא: just as 'שכר' by a נזיר means wine, so here 'שכר' means wine too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That is why the תנא קמא (step 9) used 'שכר' only to define a measure of wine, and did not add other drinks.

keyTerms.meaning: the first (unnamed) תנא in the ברייתא
we learn (by comparison)
one who takes a vow to abstain from wine

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
We learn "intoxicating drink" here from "intoxicating drink" stated about a nazirite.
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places. במדבר 6:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 17 by explaining the תנא קמא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא uses a גזירה שוה from נזיר, so 'שכר' here means wine.

steps.title: רבי יהודה does not learn from נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה does not accept the גזירה שוה from נזיר, so he reads 'שכר' as other intoxicating drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה does not learn 'שכר' from 'שכר' of נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה: without the comparison to נזיר, 'שכר' is free to mean drinks other than wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains steps 12-15. Since 'שכר' means other drinks, 'יין' had to be written separately, and it teaches that only wine brings מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: does not learn (does not accept the comparison)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda does not learn
"intoxicating drink" from "intoxicating drink" of a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer to step 17, now explaining רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה rejects the גזירה שוה, so 'שכר' refers to other intoxicants.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: 'שכר' means 'something that intoxicates'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'שכר' as a description: wine drunk in a way that actually intoxicates.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר holds: What is 'שכר'? Something that makes a person drunk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes by explaining רבי אלעזר: 'שכר' is not a separate drink. It describes the wine as something that intoxicates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why רבי אלעזר exempted someone who paused or added water (step 16). Such drinking is not the intoxicating way, so it does not fit the word 'שכר.'

keyTerms.meaning: something, a thing
makes drunk, intoxicates

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of 'שכר.' The תנא קמא says it means wine (learned from נזיר). רבי יהודה says it means other intoxicants, which carry only an אזהרה. רבי אלעזר says it means wine drunk in its intoxicating way.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar holds:
What is "intoxicating drink"?
Something that intoxicates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר: מַאי ״שֵׁכָר״? מִידֵּי דְּהוּא מְשַׁכֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to step 17 by explaining רבי אלעזר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת depends on how each תנא reads 'שכר': as wine (from נזיר), as other intoxicants, or as wine drunk in an intoxicating manner.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר reads 'שכר' as describing wine drunk in the way that intoxicates, not as a separate drink.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא about figs, honey and milk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that a כהן who ate a sweet fig or drank honey or milk and then served gets מלקות, and asks whose opinion it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow: someone who ate a dried fig from קעילה, or drank honey or milk, then went into the מקדש and served, gets lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks which of the three תנאים it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא punishes a כהן for things that are not wine at all. That only makes sense for a תנא who counts other intoxicating foods as 'שכר'.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
A dried fig from the place called קעילה
He did the עבודה (Temple service)
He gets lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom is that which is taught:
one who ate a dried fig from Ke'ila,
phrases.notes: These figs were very sweet and could make a person drunk.

phrases.english: or drank honey or milk,
and entered the Temple and served, he is flogged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the three-way מחלוקת just explained to an outside ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the ברייתא about figs, honey and milk follows.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא matches רבי יהודה, who includes any intoxicating food in the איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? רבי יהודה's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי יהודה reads 'שכר' as any intoxicating thing, not just wine (Step 19). So a fig, honey or milk can make a כהן חייב only by his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? (whose view is it)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who includes all intoxicants.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אחותאי rules like רבי אלעזר, and notes that רב called רבי אלעזר 'the most fortunate of the חכמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אחותאי said: the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר. And רב called רבי אלעזר 'the happiest of the חכמים'.
steps.whatsHappening: After the three opinions, the גמרא gives the practical ruling: we follow רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר is the most lenient: a כהן is only חייב for wine drunk in an intoxicating way, all at once and with no water added. רב's praise shows how fully the הלכה goes with him.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows this person
The most fortunate (praised) of the Sages

steps.whatToRemember: Practical הלכה: a כהן who drank wine but paused or added water is פטור, like רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Aḥotai says:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.
And Rav would call Rabbi Elazar:
"The most fortunate of the Sages."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אֲחוֹתַאי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the מחלוקת between the three תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר: only undiluted wine drunk in one go makes the כהן חייב.

steps.title: רב אשי will not release a נדר after drinking wine
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא of הוצל came to have his נדר about his wife released, and רב אשי told him to come back tomorrow, because רב would not teach on a יום טוב after drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא of הוצל had made a נדר against his wife. He came to רב אשי, who said: 'Go now and come back tomorrow, because רב would not set up an אמורא to teach from one יום טוב meal until the next day, because of drunkenness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the rule that someone who drank wine may not give a halachic ruling. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי had drunk wine, so he would not release the נדר that day. He brings proof from רב, who stopped public teaching on יום טוב because of the wine at the meal.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a vow
His wife
The speaker who loudly repeated the רב's lecture to the crowd
יום טוב, a festival day
Drunkenness

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not a כהן going into the מקדש. The same פרשה also forbids giving halachic rulings after wine, and releasing a נדר counts as a ruling.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא דְּהוּצָל הֲוָה נִידְרָא עֲלַהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ,
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa of Huzal had vowed against his wife,
phrases.notes: He had vowed not to benefit from her, and wanted the vow released.

phrases.english: he came before Rav Ashi.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל הָאִידָּנָא וְתָא לִמְחַר,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go now and come back tomorrow,
for Rav would not place a speaker before him
from one festival day to the next, because of drunkenness.
phrases.notes: He means from the יום טוב meal until the next morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא דְּהוּצָל הֲוָה נִידְרָא עֲלַהּ דְּבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a practical story about wine and giving rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who drank wine should not give a halachic ruling, such as releasing a נדר.

steps.title: But you diluted your wine with water
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא asks: רב ruled like רבי אלעזר that adding water removes the איסור, and you put water in your wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But רב said the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר, and you, sir, put water in your wine!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges רב אשי's refusal, using the ruling from Step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, wine mixed with any water does not count as intoxicating. Since רב אשי diluted his wine, it seems he should be allowed to rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (start of a challenge)
Master, a respectful 'you'
Puts water into it (dilutes the wine)

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't Rav say:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר הוּא דְּקָא רָמֵי בֵּיהּ מַיָּא!
phrases.english: and the Master is one who puts water into it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's behavior in Step 24 using the הלכה in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's refusal to rule after drinking diluted wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the הלכה is like רבי אלעזר, diluted wine does not count, so רב אשי should be allowed to rule.

steps.title: Water only helps for a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers: רבי אלעזר's leniency is for exactly a רביעית; I drank more than a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That is not a problem. That ruling is for a רביעית; this case is more than a רביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by limiting רבי אלעזר's leniency to a certain amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding water only takes away the איסור when someone drank just a רביעית. With more than a רביעית, a little water does not stop a person from becoming drunk, so רב אשי still could not rule.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not a difficulty
A quarter-לוג, the basic amount for the איסור
More than a רביעית

steps.whatToRemember: Diluting helps only for a רביעית. If someone drank more than that, water does not make him fit to rule.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is not difficult:
that is with a quarter-log,
phrases.notes: 'That' is רבי אלעזר's ruling; 'this' is what רב אשי himself drank.

phrases.english: this is with more than a quarter-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בִּרְבִיעִית, הָא בְּיוֹתֵר מִכְּדֵי רְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any added water removes the איסור, no matter how much was drunk.
steps.terutzMaskana: Water helps only for a רביעית; with more than a רביעית the person is still considered drunk.

steps.title: 'ולהבדיל בין הקדש ובין החול' means דמין, ערכין, חרמין and הקדשות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins explaining the פסוק after the איסור of wine: separating between קודש and חול refers to the laws of דמין, ערכין, חרמין and הקדשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And to separate between the holy and the ordinary', these are דמין and ערכין, חרמין and הקדשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא on the next פסוק in the wine פרשה. It lists which topics one may not rule on after drinking wine, and it sets up more teachings to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק right after the איסור of wine speaks about separating holy from ordinary. The ברייתא reads it as halachic rulings about things dedicated to the מקדש, which a person who drank wine should not decide.

keyTerms.meaning: And to separate (to tell apart)
Vowing to give the market value of a person
Vowing to give a person's fixed value set by the תורה
Property dedicated as חרם
Things consecrated to the מקדש

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And that you may differentiate between the sacred and the common":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:10

phrases.english: these are values and valuations,
dedications and consecrations.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וּלְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבֵין הַחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: which rulings are forbidden after drinking wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Separating between holy and ordinary' refers to rulings about דמין, ערכין, חרמין and הקדשות.

steps.title: The rest of the verse: what else a drunk person may not teach
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא keeps explaining the פסוק word by word: טומאה and טהרה, הוראה, מדרשות, הלכה and תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Between the impure and the pure' means the laws of טומאה and טהרה. 'And to teach' means giving a practical ruling. 'All the statutes' means the מדרשות. 'Which ה׳ spoke' means הלכה. 'By the hand of משה' means תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from step 27, going through each phrase of the פסוק and listing more areas of Torah that a person who drank wine may not teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק is tied to a different kind of Torah knowledge. Together they build a full list of what is off limits after drinking wine. The next steps will ask how far this list really goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The laws of ritual impurity and purity
Giving a practical halachic ruling
Laws learned out from the words of the Torah
Here: a law given orally to משה at סיני
The reasoning and discussion behind the laws

phrases.english: "Between the impure and the pure" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:10-11. This is the same set of פסוקים as step 27.

phrases.english: these are the laws of impurity and purity.
"And to teach" – this is giving a ruling.
"All the statutes" – these are the expositions.
"Which the Lord spoke" – this is halacha.
phrases.notes: Here הלכה means a law handed down orally from משה at סיני.

phrases.english: "By the hand of Moshe" – this is Talmud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּין הַטָּמֵא וּבֵין הַטָּהוֹר אֵלּוּ טְמָאוֹת וּטְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 27, which began explaining the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who drank wine may not teach טומאה and טהרה, give הוראה, or teach מדרשות, הלכה or תלמוד.

steps.title: Teaching משנה is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says teaching משנה after drinking is permitted, because the פסוק says 'to teach', meaning practical rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think even teaching משנה is forbidden. So the פסוק says 'and to teach', which means only practical rulings are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now narrows the list: teaching משנה is not included in the איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ולהורות shows that the איסור is about giving practical rulings. משנה is not used directly to rule, so teaching it is allowed. Note that the תנא קמא still forbids teaching תלמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have thought' — sets up a possibility that the פסוק rejects
'The verse teaches' — introduces the proof from the פסוק
The basic teachings of the תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'תלמוד לומר' (meaning 'the verse says') with the word תלמוד in the list before it (the reasoning behind the laws). Same word, two different uses.

phrases.english: One might think even the Mishnah is included?
The verse teaches: "And to teach."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the list given in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching משנה after drinking wine is permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה: even תלמוד is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה goes further: even teaching תלמוד is allowed, and only giving an actual ruling is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: You might think even teaching תלמוד is forbidden. So the פסוק says 'and to teach', meaning only actual rulings are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא disagrees with the first and allows even more teaching after drinking wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbade תלמוד, since practical rulings come out of it. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה uses the same word ולהורות to say that only an actual ruling is forbidden. Teaching the discussion behind it is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: The reasoning behind the laws, which practical conclusions can come from

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: משנה is allowed, תלמוד is forbidden. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: even תלמוד is allowed, and only an actual הוראה is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehudah says:
One might think even Talmud is included?
The verse teaches: "And to teach."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר יָכוֹל אַף תַּלְמוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of step 29 and allows teaching תלמוד too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching תלמוד after drinking wine is permitted; only giving an actual ruling is forbidden.

steps.title: Whose view allows ruling on a שרץ and a frog?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person who drank wine may say that a שרץ is טמא and a frog is טהור. The גמרא suggests this follows only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow: 'Excluded are a שרץ, which is טמא, and a frog, which is טהור, since people who drank wine may rule about them.' Should we say it follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה and not the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא and tries to work out which side of the argument it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a שרץ is טמא sounds like a ruling, yet the ברייתא allows it after drinking. The גמרא suggests this fits only the lenient view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. If so, the חכמים would disagree with this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose view does it follow?'
A creeping creature whose dead body is טמא
A frog, whose dead body is טהור
People who drank wine
'Shall we say' — a suggestion the גמרא may reject

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow, which was taught in a baraita:
Excluded are: a sheretz is impure, and a frog is pure,
phrases.notes: 'Excluded' means these cases are left out of the איסור.

phrases.english: for people who drank wine may give a ruling about them.

phrases.aramaic: נֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Shall we say it is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehudah,
and not the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the argument in steps 29-30 to decide who a new ברייתא follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the ברייתא about the שרץ and the frog follow only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?

steps.title: Even the Rabbis agree: basic facts are not a ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא can fit the חכמים too, because such basic facts are learned by schoolchildren and do not count as a ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the חכמים. This case is different, because it is something you could go and learn in a children's school.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion in step 31 and shows the ברייתא works for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something every schoolchild knows, like a שרץ being טמא, is not a real הוראה. So even the stricter חכמים would allow a drunk person to say it. The ברייתא does not prove anything about the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say' — shows the source fits the other view too
'Here it is different'
'Go read it in school' — something obvious that everyone learns

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Rabbis,
and here it is different,
since it is a matter of 'go read it in the schoolhouse.'
phrases.notes: בי רב here means a children's school. It is so basic that saying it is not really giving a ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 31's suggestion that only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה could hold this.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the ברייתא proves it follows only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Basic, well-known facts are not a הוראה at all, so even the חכמים allow them.

steps.title: רב rules like רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: teaching is allowed, but ruling is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's practical ruling on the argument from steps 29-30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the הלכה, after drinking one may teach even תלמוד, and only giving a real ruling is forbidden. This sets up a question about how רב himself behaved.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The הלכה follows...' — a final practical ruling

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: Rav said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehudah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the argument in steps 29-30 and decides it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: teaching is allowed after drinking, and only ruling is forbidden.

steps.title: But רב himself stopped lecturing on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if teaching is allowed, why did רב not lecture with an אמורא on יום טוב because of drinking?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב would not put up an אמורא from the יום טוב meal until the next day because of drunkenness!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling using his own behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allows teaching after drinking, yet he himself stopped his public lecture on יום טוב. This looks like his practice goes against his own ruling. It is the same fact רב אשי mentioned in step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who repeated the teacher's lecture aloud to the crowd
Drunkenness
יום טוב

phrases.english: But Rav would not set up an amora
phrases.notes: This is the speaker who repeated the lecture out loud so the whole crowd could hear.

phrases.english: from one day of Yom Tov to the next
phrases.notes: He means from the יום טוב meal until the next morning.

phrases.english: because of drunkenness!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that teaching after drinking is allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If teaching is allowed, רב should not have needed to stop lecturing on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב was different: he gave rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's lectures included practical rulings, which are forbidden after drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב is different, because he used to give rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב's own practice does not go against his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching is allowed, but רב's lectures were not just teaching; they included הוראה. Since הוראה is forbidden after drinking even by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, רב had to stop.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is different'
He would give practical rulings

phrases.english: Rav is different, since he would give rulings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 34.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: רב's lectures included rulings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב stopped teaching, which looks like he forbade teaching.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב stopped because his lectures included הוראה, which is forbidden.

steps.title: Then let him lecture without ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes again: רב could have lectured and simply not given rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him put up an אמורא and just not give rulings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 35.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the rulings were a problem, רב could have kept teaching and avoided ruling. So why stop the whole lecture?

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him set up' (the אמורא)

phrases.english: Let him set one up and not give rulings!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב stopped because he gave rulings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He could have taught without ruling, so stopping completely was not needed.

steps.title: Wherever רב sat, rulings followed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב could never teach without people asking him for rulings and him giving them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever רב sat, it was impossible for him without giving a ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer that explains רב's behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רב, teaching and ruling could not be kept apart. Any lecture of his would turn into practical rulings. So to avoid ruling while drunk, he had to stop teaching altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was not possible for him'
'Wherever'

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that teaching after drinking is allowed. רב only stopped himself because his teaching always led to real rulings.

phrases.english: Wherever Rav sits,
it is not possible for him without giving a ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּיָתֵיב רַב לָא סַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּלָא הוֹרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 36 and closes the discussion of רב's practice.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: for רב, teaching always led to ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב could teach and hold back from ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב, teaching without ruling was not possible, so he stopped completely.

steps.title: One bite, four sin offerings and one guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that a single act of eating can make a person bring four חטאות and one אשם. The case is a טמא person who eats חלב that is also נותר from קדשים, on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Sometimes a person eats just one time and must bring four sin offerings and one guilt offering. For example, an impure person ate forbidden fat that was also leftover meat from a holy offering, and he ate it on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a case where one bite of food breaks many different איסורים at the same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single piece of food carries four separate חטאת prohibitions: חלב, נותר, eating קדשים while טמא, and eating on יום הכיפורים. Because the fat comes from a holy offering, eating it is also מעילה, misuse of holy property, which brings an אשם. The point is that one action can count as many separate sins.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering, brought for doing by mistake a sin that would bring כרת if done on purpose
A guilt offering; here it is the one brought for מעילה, using holy property
Forbidden fat of an animal
Meat of an offering left over after the time allowed for eating it
Holy things, offerings that belong to the בית המקדש
Ritually impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic rule of קרבנות: when one action breaks several separate איסורים, each one can bring its own korban.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There is one who eats a single act of eating
and they are liable for it four sin offerings
and one guilt offering:
an impure person who ate forbidden fat,
and it was leftover meat from holy offerings,
on יום הכיפורים.
phrases.notes: Count them: fat, leftover, eating holy food while impure, and eating on יום הכיפורים make four. The guilt offering is for using holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ אוֹכֵל אֲכִילָה אַחַת וְחַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ אַרְבָּעָה חַטָּאוֹת וְאָשָׁם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It has nothing to do with the earlier discussion about רב teaching after drinking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One act of eating can make a person liable for four חטאות (חלב, נותר, טומאה, יום הכיפורים) and one אשם (מעילה).

steps.title: רבי מאיר adds a fifth sin offering for carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that if this happened on שבת and the person carried the food out to a public area, he brings another חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: If it was שבת and he carried the food out, he is liable for that too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר adds to the list in the משנה. If the day was also שבת and the eater carried the food from one domain to another, he would owe one more חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר wants to make the case even bigger by adding the מלאכה of הוצאה on שבת. Then the same piece of food leads to five חטאות instead of four. This sets up the argument with the חכמים in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sabbath, when doing מלאכה is forbidden
He carried it out from a private area to a public area, the מלאכה of הוצאה
Liable, here meaning he must bring another חטאת

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
If it was Shabbat
and he carried it out, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה שַׁבָּת וְהוֹצִיאוֹ – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more liability to the case in step 38.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the eating also happened on שבת and he carried the food out, he owes an extra חטאת for הוצאה.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the addition because carrying is a different kind of sin
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell רבי מאיר that the שבת חטאת does not belong in this list, because it is not part of the same kind of sin as the eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That is not from the same category.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי מאיר. The person really does owe for carrying on שבת, but it should not be counted in this list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is listing liabilities that come from the act of eating itself. Carrying on שבת comes from a different action, so it is "not from the same name." The חכמים do not say he is free from the שבת חטאת. They only say it doesn't belong in a list about one act of eating.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not of the same name or category, meaning a different kind of sin

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are NOT saying the person is free from a חטאת for carrying on שבת. They agree he owes it. They only say it does not count as part of this one act of eating.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה counts only sins that come from the eating itself: four חטאות and one אשם. רבי מאיר wants to add carrying on שבת, and the חכמים leave it out because it is a different kind of act.

phrases.english: They said to him:
It is not from the same category.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's addition in step 39.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects counting the שבת liability inside the list of liabilities from the one act of eating. It does not reject the liability itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Carrying is a different kind of act from eating, so it does not belong in a count of what the eating causes.
